newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles district attorney race too close to call.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles district attorney race too close to call.

text.p: Los Angeles District Attorney Gil Garcetti held a slim lead over his opponent as votes continued to be counted early Wednesday in a race dominated by the unsuccessful murder prosecution of former football star O.J. Simpson.

Garcetti, looking for a second four-year term as head of an agency with more than 1,000 prosecutors and a budget of $170 million, held a 50 percent to 49.9 percent lead over John Lynch with about two thirds of the vote counted.

Garcetti became America's best known district attorney thanks to the Simpson trial, but the result of the trial, in which Simpson was found not guilty of murdering his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, dogged him throughout his campaign.

Lynch, an influential assistant district attorney in charge of the city's suburban Norwalk office, hammered away during his campaign on Garcetti's failure to get guilty verdicts in the Simpson trial, claiming he put incompetent prosecutors on the case and then gave them huge bonuses despite their failure to convict the former football star.

The tactic appeared to be paying off during the early vote counting on Tuesday night, with Lynch taking a 55 percent to 45 percent lead. But Garcetti then took a slim lead of 50 percent to 49.9 percent in a race that was too close to call.

Garcetti reportedly spent $1.3 million on his campaign compared to Lynch's $350,000. Lynch accused the incumbent of giving voters "a million dollars of lies" in an intensive and divisive advertising campaign.

Lynch also pointed to Garcetti's other high profile failures, including the trial of four white police officers found not guilty in state court of beating black motorist Rodney King after they were captured on videotape raining blows on him.
The acquittal sparked deadly street riots in Los Angeles, and two of the men were later convicted in federal court.

In addition there was a year-long child molestation investigation against pop star Michael Jackson which ended in 1994 with no charges filed, Another case was the acquittal of rap star Snoop Doggy Dogg and his bodyguard on murder charges earlier this year; a trial Garcetti had promised would end with guilty verdicts.

Garcetti countered in his campaign by portraying Lynch as an insensitive bureaucrat, uninterested in issues like spousal and child abuse that Garcetti has championed, setting up task forces to combat such abuses. He has also set up an anti-gang task force.
In the March primary, Garcetti was forced into a runoff election after he picked up only 37 percent of the vote to Lynch's 21 percent.
